text:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — we need a tight set of rebuttals vs cloud AI platforms, LLM API startups, and infra vendors. Outputs by EOD Tue: (1) 3x concise one-liners per opponent, (2) 3-line benchmark narrative we can use in press/webinar, (3) webinar hook (30s elevator). Field/AEs need callouts for routing. Starting notes:

Liam Chen: +1. Focus on predictable economics and routing fallbacks. Customers care about 'what happens at 10x load'. Keep cost claims defensible.

Devon Ortiz: For each opponent: problem, our claim, supporting metric. Example:
Cloud AI platforms — problem: opaque burst pricing; claim: predictable per-token unit economics with reserved capacity; metric: 40–60% lower 95th-pctl token cost in our Dedicated runs vs comparable managed endpoints (internal perf bench).

Sofia Ramirez: Field needs short rebut templates. e.g., "If prospect says 'we already use CloudX endpoints' -> 'Are you seeing predictable latency and a cost SLO at 10k TPS? We can show a side-by-side with reserved capacity and routing policies.'" :thinking_face:

Ava Brooks: Can we get a 1‑pager with suggested probing questions for AEs? Also routing mapping for inbound: small leads -> self-serve play; mid-market -> SDR; enterprise + security reqs -> AE/SE.

Devon Ortiz: Draft benchmark narrative suggestion:
"Redwood's benchmarks emphasize tail latency, unit cost, and graceful degradation. In our Dedicated configs, we maintain sub-150ms median latency for common prompts while lowering per‑token cost via intelligent batching and prefix caching — delivering predictable economics teams can budget against."

Maya Patel: Webinar hook ideas (30s):
"We used to think model access was the hard part. Today the competitive edge is serving — making great models economical and reliable under real traffic. In this session we'll show live comparisons, failover demos, and the playbook teams use to turn inference into a predictable product cost."

Sofia Ramirez: Routing rules snippet — feel free to edit for implementation:
```yaml
rules:
  - if: buyer_size >= 1000 OR compliance == 'required'
    route: field/enterprise
  - if: wants_private_deploy == true
    route: field/solutions
  - if: trial_usage > 50k_tokens/day
    route: growth/sdr
  - else:
    route: self-serve/onboarding
```

Devon Ortiz: Sales rebut snippets (1–2 lines each):
- Cloud API: "Cloud APIs are fast to start. When you need predictable cost/throughput, teams move to reserved capacity — we make that transition frictionless."
- LLM API startups: "They optimize for model access; we optimize for serving economics and SLAs in production."
- Infra vendors: "They give you runtime primitives; we give you an opinionated, observable stack and playbooks to keep apps live during real traffic patterns."

content-bot: Suggested assets to link: https://drive.redwood/benchmarks/2026-inference-summary.pdf, https://notebook.redwood/webinar/failover-demo

Maya Patel: Action items:
- Devon: turn the benchmarking paragraph into 2 short web blurbs (due Tue EOD)
- Sofia: build 1‑pager rebut quicksheet for AEs (due Mon)
- Liam: pack 3 webinar demo ideas and owner (due Fri)
- Ava: align SDR routing with rules above and add 3 probing Qs (due Mon)

Liam Chen: I'll own the demo 'failover to cheaper variant' and 'tail-latency under burst'.

Ava Brooks: Got it — SDR playbook will include the probing Qs and an objection card.

Maya Patel: Great. If anyone has phrasing that sounds too 'marketing-y', post it here and we'll tighten. :thumbsup:

Devon Ortiz: Posting first pass of 3 web blurbs in the doc later today.

Sofia Ramirez: Will mock the AE quicksheet layout and drop screenshots of the rebut lines.

Maya Patel: Thanks team — we'll review progress in Thursday standup.
